lesson: Card #7 was 0W-5L for -$70.47 — the worst day yet, and every single pick was a straight win bet on a team simply rated stronger on paper. West Brom drew, Palace lost at home, Mainz got beaten, Osasuna were shut out, and the Strasbourg-Monaco goals bet fell one goal short. Digging into today's fixtures turned up a clear reason to slow down rather than push harder: Le Mans' opponent today, Lens, is priced as a 57% favourite by the model but has actually lost its last two league games. That's the exact same mistake as yesterday — a name/table-position favourite whose recent results don't back it up. Today's card is deliberately small.

matches.analysis: FEATURED MATCH. City are the only team on today's board with a genuinely spotless recent record: three wins from three, with real margins (2-1, 4-1, 1-0), not scraped results. United have been solid but not dominant — a 2-2 home draw with Everton, though also a 5-2 win at Ipswich. Given how many favourites fell yesterday, the bar here was deliberately high, and City's is the one case where the form is completely unblemished rather than just table position.

The model has Lens as clear favourites (57%), but they've actually lost their last two league games (1-2 at Strasbourg, 0-1 at home to Lorient) after an opening 5-2 win. That's a favourite on paper contradicted by current form — precisely the pattern that cost us yesterday. Pass, and a useful reminder to check actual recent results before trusting a model probability at face value.

Celta are favourites at home, but they haven't won in their last three games (two draws, one defeat to Athletic Bilbao) and haven't looked sharp doing it. Backing them here would be the same mistake we're trying to avoid today — a table-position pick without current form behind it. Pass.
A genuine three-way coin flip on the model (34/31/35). Nothing here to back with conviction. Pass.

avoid: RB Leipzig vs Hamburg and Elversberg vs Bayern (Bundesliga), and Brest vs PSG (Ligue 1) — all three favourites are priced under 1.30, far too short to offer value regardless of how likely they are to win • After yesterday's 0-5, today's card is intentionally one bet, not padded out to make up for it. Chasing yesterday's loss with more volume today would be exactly the wrong response.
